Combative

kuhm-BAT-iv · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Combative is ready or eager to fight or argue.

The union representative grew visibly combative the moment management floated a pay freeze during contract talks.

Worked Example

Ever since the trade fell through, the two general managers have traded combative statements in every press interview.

Combative describes a readiness to fight -- verbally or physically -- rather than a single angry outburst.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

quarrelsome: given to arguing

contentious: likely to cause disagreement

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

amicable: friendly and without hard feelings

conciliatory: intended to calm anger or make peace

Where it sits · how close to open hostility it comes — assertive → combative → belligerent

assertive vs. combative: Assertive simply means confidently stating one's views, without necessarily the eagerness to fight that combative implies.

belligerent vs. combative: Belligerent goes further than combative, describing outright hostility, often on the edge of actual violence.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — com-

prefix — com-: with, together (before b, m, p) (Latin)

root — bat-

root — bat-: to beat, to fight (Latin battuere)

suffix — -ive

suffix — -ive: tending to, having the nature of (Latin (-ivus))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin com- ('together') plus battuere ('to beat, to fight') plus -ive ('tending to') -- combative describes someone tending toward a fight. The same root gives us the everyday word battle.

Use the root in a new word: battle

Word Choice

Combative can describe physical fighting, but it's used just as often for verbal sparring -- a combative interview, a combative tone, or a combative negotiator.
